title: Warning symptoms reported
user-facing text: You reported a warning sign (for example chest pain, fainting, unusual breathlessness, or a doctor's advice to limit activity). Please see a doctor before starting an exercise programme. Baymax will not generate a plan until you update your answers after that visit.

title: Heart condition: readiness questions not answered
applies when: answered eq false AND classification eq Cardiac
user-facing text: Because you have a heart condition, please answer the exercise readiness questions (including whether your doctor has cleared you) before a plan is made.

title: Heart condition without a doctor's clearance
applies when: answered eq true AND classification eq Cardiac AND clearance ne true
user-facing text: With a heart condition, a doctor should clear you for exercise first. Once they have, update your readiness answers and your plan will be generated.

title: Heart disease listed but classification differs
applies when: answered eq true AND conditions contains Heart Disease AND classification ne Cardiac AND clearance ne true
user-facing text: You listed heart disease. A doctor should clear you for exercise before a plan is generated.

title: Weight missing
applies when: answered eq true AND weightKg lt 1
user-facing text: Your weight is missing; intensity and energy estimates depend on it. Please add it in your profile.

title: Height missing
applies when: answered eq true AND heightCm lt 1
user-facing text: Your height is missing, so your BMI-based rules cannot be applied. Please add it in your profile.

title: Date of birth missing
applies when: answered eq true AND ageRecorded eq false
user-facing text: Your date of birth is missing; several safety rules depend on age. Please add it in your profile.

title: Heart condition
effect: excludeImpact=high; excludeTags=hiit|isometric|plyo; maxLevel=2; maxDays=4; maxSessionMin=30; modify externalLoad: Use a light weight you could lift about 15 times, breathe out as you lift and never hold your breath
user-facing text: Heart condition: only low-impact, steady-effort exercise is included — no maximal-effort or breath-holding work. Get your doctor's clearance before starting, and stop immediately if you feel chest pain, dizziness or unusual breathlessness.

title: Hypertension
effect: excludeImpact=high; excludeTags=hiit|plyo; maxLevel=2; maxDays=5; maxHoldSeconds=20; modify externalLoad: Use a light weight you could lift about 15 times, breathe out as you lift and never hold your breath
user-facing text: Hypertension: high-intensity intervals and high-impact moves are removed, and static holds (planks, wall sits) are capped at 20 seconds. Breathe steadily and never hold your breath — straining raises blood pressure. Check with your doctor about the right intensity for you.

title: Diabetes
user-facing text: Diabetes: sessions are steady and moderate. Check your blood sugar before and after exercise, keep fast-acting carbohydrates nearby, and ask your doctor before training on an empty stomach.

title: Asthma
user-facing text: Asthma: high-intensity intervals are removed. Warm up thoroughly and keep your reliever inhaler with you.

title: BMI 30 or above
user-facing text: BMI {bmi}: jumping and running-style moves are replaced with low-impact options to protect your knees and ankles.

title: BMI 25 or above
user-facing text: Jump (plyometric) exercises are removed to reduce joint stress at your current weight.

title: BMI below 18.5
user-facing text: Underweight BMI: the plan focuses on strength training and limits cardio so you do not burn the energy you need to gain healthy weight.

title: Age 55 or above
user-facing text: Age 55+: high-impact moves are removed as a precaution.

title: Age 65 or above
user-facing text: Age 65+: balance training is added, as WHO recommends for older adults.

title: Sedentary starting point
user-facing text: You are starting from a sedentary baseline, so sessions are shorter and exercises are beginner-friendly. Increase gradually.

title: Knee injury or pain
user-facing text: Knee: high-impact moves that load the knee are left out, and other knee exercises carry a pain-free-range reminder. See a physiotherapist if the pain persists.

title: Lower back injury or pain
user-facing text: Lower back: high-impact moves that load the back are left out, and back exercises carry a pain-free-range reminder.

title: Shoulder injury or pain
user-facing text: Shoulder: pressing exercises carry a pain-free-range reminder.

title: Wrist injury or pain
user-facing text: Wrist: exercises that put weight on your hands carry a reminder to use your fists or forearms, or skip them if they hurt.

title: Ankle injury or pain
user-facing text: Ankle: jumping and running moves are left out.

title: Obese

title: At-Risk
effect: maxBand=moderate; aerobic 150-300 min/week; strength 2+ days; stretching 2+ days
user-facing text: A gentle start at moderate effort, increased step by step as you get fitter.

title: Diabetic
effect: maxBand=vigorous; aerobic 150-300 min/week; strength 2+ days; stretching 2+ days; max 2 rest days in a row
user-facing text: Activity spread across the week, with no more than two days in a row without exercise, plus strength training.

title: Cardiac
effect: maxBand=moderate; aerobic 150-300 min/week; strength 2+ days; stretching 2+ days
user-facing text: Steady, low-impact aerobic work at a moderate effort. Follow the advice of your doctor or cardiac rehabilitation team.
You reported no condition, but Module 2's screening model puts people like you at higher than average risk, so your plan starts at a moderate effort. This is a screening estimate, not a diagnosis.
PCOS: regular aerobic activity and strength training on two or more days a week are recommended. Your plan follows the same weekly targets.
Module 2 rated your health risk as high: build up slowly and talk to your doctor before increasing the effort.
